### Building a New PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order to avoid mistakes. | # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips | |---|------------|----------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Decide what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) and set a budget. | Use online PC builders (PCPartPicker, BuildMyPC) to compare prices and check compatibility. | | 2 | **Choose Components** | Pick CPU, motherboard, RAM, GPU, storage, PSU, case, cooling, and peripherals. | • **CPU + Motherboard**: Match socket (e.g., Intel LGA 1700, AMD AM5).
• **RAM**: DDR5/DDR4, 16 GB is a good baseline.
• **GPU**: Depends on workload; 3060/3070 for gaming, RTX 4090 for 4K.
• **Storage**: NVMe SSD for OS + SSD/HDD combo for bulk.
• **PSU**: 80+ Gold, 650–850 W (or more for high‑end GPUs).
• **Case**: ATX mid‑tower, ensure airflow and cable management. | | 3 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | You’ll need a Phillips‑head screwdriver, anti‑static wrist strap (optional), cable ties, and a clean, flat surface. | Work on a non‑conductive surface (wood or plastic table). | | 4 | **Prepare the Case** | Remove side panels, lay the case upside down. | Keep screws handy; they’re usually labeled. | | 5 | **Install the Power Supply** | Slide PSU into its tray, secure with screws, route cables. | Make sure the fan faces the intake or exhaust as per case design. | | 6 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Align standoffs with holes, screw in lightly. | Don’t overtighten; leave a little wiggle for cable routing. | | 7 | **Install the CPU** | Open the socket latch, align the CPU (triangle marker), gently place it, lock latch. | Avoid touching pins; use a soft cloth. | | 8 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler** | If cooler isn’t pre‑applied, spread a pea‑size amount. Attach cooler, secure. | For air coolers, follow the mounting kit. For liquid coolers, attach pump to motherboard. | | 9 | **Insert RAM** | Snap sticks into DIMM slots, ensuring they click. | Install in pairs for dual‑channel (e.g., slots 1 & 3). | | 10 | **Mount Storage** | Secure SSD/HDD in drive bays or M.2 slot. | For M.2, use the screw provided with the motherboard. | | 11 | **Install the GPU** | Remove the appropriate expansion slot cover, insert GPU, secure with screws. | Connect PCIe power cables from PSU to GPU. | | 12 | **Connect Power Cables** | 24‑pin ATX to motherboard, 8‑pin EPS to CPU, PCIe power to GPU, SATA power to drives. | Double‑check each connector is fully seated. | | 13 | **Cable Management** | Route cables through the case’s cable‑management holes, tie them with cable ties. | Keep airflow unobstructed; route cables away from fans. | | 14 | **Double‑Check Connections** | Verify all screws, cables, and components are secure. | Look for any loose screws that could short. | | 15 | **Close the Case** | Replace side panels, screw in. | Ensure no cables are pinched. | | 16 | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Connect monitor, keyboard, power on. Enter BIOS (usually F2, DEL). | Set boot priority to your OS drive, enable XMP for RAM. | | 17 | **Install Operating System** | Boot from USB/DVD, install Windows/macOS/Linux. | Keep drivers handy; install motherboard chipset drivers first. | | 18 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | GPU drivers, chipset, audio, network. | Use manufacturer’s website or Windows Update. | | 19 | **Test Stability** | Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark, Cinebench). | Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor, MSI Afterburner). | | 20 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep drivers updated, clean dust every 3–6 months. | Use a static‑free mat if you’re sensitive to static. | --- #### Quick Checklist - [ ] CPU + Cooler - [ ] Motherboard + Standoffs - [ ] RAM - [ ] GPU - [ ] Storage (SSD/HDD) - [ ] PSU - [ ] Case - [ ] Cables (SATA, PCIe, 24‑pin, 8‑pin) - [ ] Monitor, Keyboard, Mouse - [ ] Operating System media #### Common Pitfalls | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **Short circuit** | Check for stray screws, metal contacts, or misplaced standoffs. | | **No POST** | Verify CPU is seated correctly, RAM is installed in the right slots, GPU is fully inserted. | | **Overheating** | Ensure proper airflow, clean fans, apply thermal paste correctly. | | **Fan noise** | Check for dust, replace failing fans, adjust fan curves. | #### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – Build planner, price comparison, compatibility checker. - **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware. - **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community help. - **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, and GPU manuals. --- ### Final Thought Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you control over performance, aesthetics, and future upgrades. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for specific help. Happy building!
